components.text: The decisive inference from nested formal unity to a transcendent intelligent or willing being is not entailed.
Whether nested formal unity supplies an inference to a transcendent intelligent or willing God.
Whether inherited values and interpersonal structures ultimately require or indicate a divine unifying source.
Whether shared purposes and values require an ultimate transcendent unity rather than interpersonal transmission.
Whether useful patterns are objective stages in a divine hierarchy or specifically dependent on human cognition.
Whether useful patterns are mind-independent realities capable of grounding an ascent to God.
The need to infer transcendence, intelligence, or will from formal organization rather than merely establish higher-level constraint.
Whether higher-order causal constraint is adequately explained as a projection or abstraction of human minds.
Whether higher-order patterns have reality beyond useful human cognitive classification.
Whether formal organization possesses ontological and causal significance rather than being merely descriptive.
Whether Genesis's capacity to orient conduct establishes the truth or authority of its meaningful account.
Whether meaningful analogical orientation also warrants historical belief in the biblical account.
Whether analogical biblical language can refer in a disciplined way to a real event or transformation rather than merely teach detachable lessons.
Whether analogical narration can make disciplined reference to a real event or transformation.
Whether scriptural analogy is merely valuable fiction detachable from claims about reality.
Whether disciplined analogy and recurring structural correspondence can establish a singular bodily resurrection or postmortem experience.
Whether disciplined analogy alone supports singular historical and postmortem claims such as bodily resurrection.
Whether life-guiding meaning supplies evidence for a distinct historical supernatural occurrence.
Whether life-guiding analogical truth requires belief in the singular historical figures or predicted phenomena associated with it.
Whether analogical truth and life guidance require historical existence or predicted postmortem phenomena.
Whether meaningful scriptural orientation can be retained independently of supernatural historical assent.
What support makes bodily resurrection intelligible despite its additional historical and observational burden.
Whether analogical guidance can remain detached from the resurrection claim once a loving transcendent unity is accepted.
Whether resurrection must function as independent observational proof rather than coherence within prior theism.
Whether symbolic guidance exhausts what becomes intelligible once loving transcendence is accepted.
The demand for separate historical or observational support for a particular bodily resurrection and continued experience after death.
Whether personal identity can persist beyond its current material substrate in a way stronger than detachable symbolic guidance.
Whether identity's relation to changing matter makes resurrection conceptually credible despite the historical evidence demand.
Whether symbolic persistence can support more than practical guidance concerning personal continuity.
Whether persistence of a whole requires an independently existing pattern rather than a nonarbitrary structural abstraction realized in changing parts.
Whether cities and institutions can be explained through functional structure, constituent minds, and material arrangements despite downward effects.
Whether persistence through material change entails a separately existing pattern independent of human abstraction.
Whether causally useful higher-level descriptions require irreducible ontological wholes.
Whether nested purposive patterns culminate in divine unity rather than arising within a natural cognitive continuum.
Whether intelligent patterning requires substrate-independent identity rather than evolved cognitive organization.
Whether human abstraction marks an ontological discontinuity requiring higher-order mind.
Whether species-relative cognitive partitioning can account for existence when every representation of a world already occurs within mind.
Whether the dependence of conceived patterns on mind supports merely human constructivism or a more foundational priority of mind.
Whether evolutionary differences in cognition permit an account of existence conceived wholly outside mind.
Whether mind dependence demotes patterns or instead gives mind foundational ontological priority.
Whether inherited values mediated through individual minds sufficiently explain worship's formative effects without a transcendent source.
Whether shared value formation is merely transmitted or also enacted through worship toward a governing ideal.
Whether collective purposes exert formative constraint through participation in higher-order practices.
Whether culturally inherited values can sustain shared purposes without a sacred spatial and ritual center.
Whether inherited values remain socially binding without shared sacred places, practices, and purposes.
Whether bottom-up arrangements adequately explain durable communal unity and common purpose.
Whether worship's capacity to form loving or cohesive participants establishes the supernatural truth of its divine object.
Whether superior Christian social harmony, if observed, would uniquely favor God over natural causes or alternative coherent value systems.

Whether superior cohesion under Christianity would uniquely support God rather than natural social mechanisms.
